slot.brief: Match haloalkane substrates with correct elimination/substitution product or reagent behaviour (e.g. Saytzeff vs Hofmann product).

stem:
Match the reactions in Column-I with their corresponding major elimination products in Column-II.

| | Column-I | | Column-II |
|---|---|---|---|
| (A) | $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_3 + \text{alc. KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta}$ | (p) | 2-Methylbut-2-ene |
| (B) | $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa} \xrightarrow{\Delta}$ | (q) | 2-Methylbut-1-ene |
| (C) | $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + t\text{-BuO}^-\text{K}^+ \xrightarrow{\Delta}$ | (r) | But-2-ene |
| (D) | $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{alc. KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta}$ | (s) | But-1-ene |

verdicts.working: A: 2-bromobutane + alc. KOH (small base) gives Zaitsev product but-2-ene (r). B: 2-bromo-2-methylbutane + EtONa (small base) gives Zaitsev trisubstituted 2-methylbut-2-ene (p). C: same substrate with bulky t-BuOK gives Hofmann product 2-methylbut-1-ene (q). D: 1-bromobutane has only one β-carbon, giving but-1-ene (s). Matching A-r, B-p, C-q, D-s = option (A).

working:
1. Reaction (A): 2-Bromobutane undergoes dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ via an $\text{E}2$ mechanism. Following Saytzeff's rule, the more stable, more substituted alkene, but-2-ene, is formed as the major product. Hence, (A) $\rightarrow$ (r).

2. Reaction (B): 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane reacts with a small, unhindered base ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa}$). The base preferentially abstracts a proton from the more substituted $\beta$-carbon (C3), giving the more substituted Saytzeff alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene, as the major product. Hence, (B) $\rightarrow$ (p).

3. Reaction (C): 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane reacts with a bulky base, potassium *tert*-butoxide ($t\text{-BuO}^-\text{K}^+$). Due to steric hindrance, the base abstracts the more accessible $\beta$-proton from the less hindered terminal methyl group (C1), yielding the less substituted Hofmann alkene, 2-methylbut-1-ene, as the major product. Hence, (C) $\rightarrow$ (q).

4. Reaction (D): 1-Bromobutane has only one type of $\beta$-hydrogen (at C2), so elimination can only yield but-1-ene. Hence, (D) $\rightarrow$ (s).

Combining these results gives A-(r), B-(p), C-(q), D-(s).

Independent check: A: 2-bromobutane + alc. KOH (small base) gives Zaitsev product but-2-ene (r). B: 2-bromo-2-methylbutane + EtONa (small base) gives Zaitsev trisubstituted 2-methylbut-2-ene (p). C: same substrate with bulky t-BuOK gives Hofmann product 2-methylbut-1-ene (q). D: 1-bromobutane has only one β-carbon, giving but-1-ene (s). Matching A-r, B-p, C-q, D-s = option (A).
